patch.value: Update the exact-pinned pm-memory toolchain and adopt the native host mutation guard contract introduced by GH-1719 and GH-1729. Companion item: pm-cli-website-spus.

Pin all first-party tooling to npm latest and refresh the committed lockfile.; Use host actor and dry-run context at guard boundaries and preserve fail-closed behaviour.; Pass the package release gates at unchanged coverage thresholds and regenerate the changelog.; Open a dedicated PR with failure classifications and verification evidence.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text:
## SDK migration

- `TS2345` in `src/native-host.ts` and `actual CLI origin refusals retain structured codes and create remedies without retargeting aliases`. The old discovery call supplied snapshots alone. The SDK now resolves an actor from the supplied author and distinguishes previews from writes. Discovery supplies the effective author and `dry_run: true`. The locked revision guard receives the SDK's real write context.
- `portable host update publishes through the attested SDK guard`. The old preview inherited the injected client's fallback author, and SDK previews skipped mutation guards. The new preview evaluates guards on the staged tracker. Preview and publication now use the portable plan author, and the tests verify the phases and preserve refusal of foreign writes.
- `TS2339` on portable mutation options. The SDK's bulk union gained `finalize`. Portable plans now use its create/update subset, matching the persisted plan validator.
- `host publication fails closed without an in-process revision guard: foreign-missing-item`, `cross-process exact ownership at every create boundary`, `forward-only update: seeded peer operations at every import boundary`, `recovery and fresh CAS refuse newer remember edits at every journal boundary`, and `locked SDK revision refuses a concurrent foreign-field edit (host)`. Nested calls can no longer switch `cwd` or inherit hooks through a new `noExtensions` client. Fixture operations use a tracker path, foreign initialization happens outside the caller's scope, and the independent writer explicitly binds its oracle to its own active scope. [pm-cli 2026.11.23 SDK contract](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/releases/tag/v2026.11.23)
- `standalone registration reads command context once and retains every schema boundary`. The old nested client reused its caller's scope implicitly. The newer SDK ran 28 context reads. A fenced client bound to the single extension-free scope restores the one-read assertion.
- `complete SDK positives cannot be masked by a safe reference or a later local finding`, `reference boundaries inspect adjacent quoted literals and preserve pure reference twins`, and `reference terminators inspect 100000 spaces within a bounded process deadline`. The SDK accepts a complete bare environment reference and measures literal continuations, including annotations inside quoted passwords and assignment text glued to a prior value. The tests exercise separated references and attached literals under that contract. [SDK scanner behavior](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/pull/1745), [reference handling](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/pull/1746)

Exact development pins are `@unbrained/pm-cli` 2026.11.23, `pm-changelog` 2026.11.20 and `pm-ops` 2026.11.22. The peer and manifest floor follow the reviewed host.

## Upstream blockers

`compound credential control 5 remains writable and portable` and the valid-reference round trip fail because the SDK scans across string boundaries in compact JSON. `quoted scanner preserves the prior matcher corpus` also fails at full depth on an escape-only value. Both reproduce with the public SDK alone.

```js
import { scanMutationSecrets } from '@unbrained/pm-cli/sdk'

const compact = JSON.stringify({
  title: 'api_key: ${API_KEY}',
  updated: '2026-11-23T00:00:00.000Z',
})
const quote = String.fromCharCode(39)
const escapeOnly = `${quote}password${quote}: ${quote}${String.fromCharCode(92).repeat(7)}${quote}`
for (const input of [compact, escapeOnly]) {
  console.log(scanMutationSecrets(input).map(({ rule }) => rule))
}
```

2026.11.14 returns `[]` for both inputs. 2026.11.23 reports `credential_key_assignment` and `password_assignment`, respectively.

## Verification

- Initial `npm run release:check` on the earlier migration iteration ran 934 tests (919 pass, 15 fail). The diagnostic coverage snapshot was 99.98% statements, 99.67% branches, 100% functions and 99.98% lines.
- `bun install --no-save` succeeded from the committed npm lock. `bun run release:check` on the rebased code reached 425 passes, one scanner failure and two file watchdogs before switching to the scope fallback at 110 minutes. The interrupted report counted 52 cancellations.
- Direct fallback with `PM_TEST_DEPTH=quick` and two single-worker lanes recorded 236/236 SDK and CLI cases, 268/269 portable and review cases, 26/26 preview and publication cases, and 7/7 unfinished forward cases. The one failure is the valid-reference compact JSON round trip.
- The import-state and lossless export watchdogs passed under the slow-host Bun retry. The direct model retry passed 50 seeds and 2,290 SDK-read steps. Every forward case completed across the Bun run and its direct retry.
- Focused migration tests passed 74/74. The linked `pm test --run --progress` command passed 25/25. Each individual source revert failed its author, preview or registration assertion, and the three controls passed after restoring the source.
- Packed npm and Bun consumer tests passed 4/4. Build, typecheck, lint, identity, 0% duplication, docstrings, production audit (zero vulnerabilities), release attestation, isolated tracker health and validation, and the changelog check passed.
- The configured 100% coverage gate remains blocked. The full-depth quoted corpus check independently reproduced the escape-only SDK finding.

Tracker: [pm-memory-sdk-host-alignment-1122](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-memory/blob/main/.agents/pm/chores/pm-memory-sdk-host-alignment-1122.toon)

Minimal public SDK reproduction for the remaining compact scanner case: set q to String.fromCharCode(39) and ref to String.fromCharCode(36, 123) + 'BUILD_PASSWORD}'. Set title to q + 'password' + q + String.fromCharCode(58, 32) + q + ref + q. Scan JSON.stringify({ title, updated }) with updated set to an ISO timestamp. The published host reports password_assignment for the compact form and no finding when JSON.stringify uses indentation. For the separate full-depth case, use q + 'password' + q + String.fromCharCode(58, 32) + q + String.fromCharCode(92).repeat(7) + q.
